  "text": "On Monday, Sami stopped in after school and noticed the jar before he noticed the tray of honey cakes.

“Is that the marble?” he asked.

Imani nodded. “Nabil said it shouldn’t stay in a drawer.”

Sami leaned close to the glass. Then he looked at his drawing. “The fence is wrong,” he said. “Grandfather told me it had a gate.”

“It did,” her grandfather said from behind the counter. “But it never stayed shut.”

Sami pulled a pencil from his bag and began to sketch a gate on a scrap of paper. Before he finished, a woman waiting for bread pointed at the drawing beside the till. She remembered the schoolyard too, though she said the fence had been painted green. Her grandfather insisted it had always been blue. By lunchtime, three more customers had offered their versions.

Imani found a blank notebook beneath the counter. On its first page she wrote, What do you remember about the old schoolyard? She set it beside the jar with a pencil tied to the spine.

At closing time, the pages held a crooked map, two names no one could quite spell, and a story about a goat that had wandered into a classroom. Sami had drawn the goat wearing spectacles.

Her grandfather read every page while Imani wiped the tables. When he reached the map, he traced a narrow path behind the school with one floury finger.

“That’s where we played,” he said.

Imani looked at the marble, bright in its jar. “We could walk there on Saturday.”

He closed the notebook gently. “Let’s ask Nabil.”"
